title: Consolidated Compliance Opportunity Matrix and SLA Commitment Engine
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Enterprise prospects frequently submit heterogeneous security and compliance asks (SOC2 controls, ISO questionnaires, HIPAA attestation, GDPR/DPA clauses, bespoke vendor questionnaires). Current intake is manual, inconsistent across AE/CS teams, and causes slow, unpredictable SLAs for responses and evidence delivery. This creates sales friction and operational overhead for Security/Legal.

Goal: Build a product-managed pipeline that: 1) converts incoming compliance asks into a standardized 'opportunity' record, 2) scores each opportunity by combined customer risk and business value, 3) auto-enriches with evidence bundles and recommended response templates, and 4) calculates and commits a response SLA to the customer (SLA Commitment Engine) with clear escalation paths.

Scope:
- Intake sources: form submission (Sales Ops portal), gated email, enterprise questionnaire uploads (Excel/PDF), and Copy/Paste from customer vendors.
- Normalization: map asks to canonical control taxonomy (SOC2/ISO/PCI/GDPR/HIPAA) and vendor-questionnaire schema.
- Scoring: risk-to-value scoring algorithm that factors data residency/regulatory sensitivity, product access level required, contract value, and timeline pressure from the customer.
- Automation: suggest evidence bundles, pre-fill FAQ responses, surface known gaps, and compute a committed SLA (e.g., 2 business days / 10 business days) with fallback actions (escalate to Security/Legal, schedule customer call).
- Outputs: standardized opportunity record in Linear (and CRM webhook), auto-generated evidence ZIP link, PRD + reviewer checklist entry, and SLA promise sent to requester.

Out of scope for initial iteration: fully-automated legal negotiations (DPA redlines), deep legal review of custom contract clauses, and on-prem upgrade procedures.

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Median time from intake to customer SLA commit <= 48 hours for standard asks.
- Reduction in mean time-to-first-evidence delivery by 40% for common SOC2/ISO questions.
- Conversion uplift: positive impact on win rate for enterprise deals where SLA was committed (measured via CRM linkage).
- Reduction in Security/Legal manual triage volume by 50% for low/medium risk asks.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form accepts questionnaire uploads and normalizes to canonical schema for at least SOC2/ISO/GDPR/HIPAA
Automated scoring produces a numeric risk-to-value score and suggested SLA for 95% of submissions
Evidence bundle generator produces a downloadable ZIP with standardized artifacts and a provenance manifest
SLA Commitment Engine posts a human-readable SLA to the requester and creates a Linear work item with clear owner and due date
Fallback escalation rules route high-risk or ambiguous asks to Security/Legal and mark tickets as blocked with a clear next action
implementation_notes: Canonical control mapping: start with SOC2 Trust Services and ISO 27001 clauses; build mapping table in Confluence and export CSV for import

Scoring inputs: product-surface sensitivity (enum), contract ARR bands (CRM integration), data residency flag, requested timeline, question complexity (NLP classifier), and questionnaire repetition history
Evidence templates: create short-form and long-form artifacts (FAQ blurb, architecture diagram, logs retention policy, SOC2 assertion) stored in S3 with version tags
Integrations: CRM webhook to mark opportunity stage, GitHub PR template when developer work required, and pre-built Slack channel escalation hooks
Privacy/Legal: encrypt evidence bundles at rest and ensure KMS keys are recorded in manifest; add audit event for every bundle creation

open_questions: What threshold of risk-to-value score should force manual Security/Legal review vs. auto-commit? (Security prefers conservative default)
Do we expose the computed SLA in legal-facing documents, or only to the requester?
Should we allow Sales to override the auto-suggested SLA and how will overrides be audited?
How do we measure causal impact on sales outcomes (attribution to this feature vs. other GTM changes)?

Security: Finalize minimal evidence manifest schema and KMS tagging requirements

Product: Build acceptance test harness using three historical customer questionnaires and measure normalization accuracy
